scope: normal and two_busy_workers retain the earlier fixed-contour snapshot referenced by README. calibrated_tracking is the current workload and supersedes those figures for before/after comparisons.

host.load: Five sequential runs were taken while BlinkMore, the Codex service and renderer, and WindowServer were active. This is a loaded-host result, not an idle-machine guarantee.

workload.geometry: Each eye uses a changing, slightly tilted eight-point contour, subtle open-aperture variation, and two closed samples per 60-frame cycle. The cycle gives 15 synthetic bilateral closures per minute at 15 Hz.
workload.guard: The example asserts that calibration completed before timing and that warmup observed at least one blink. It black_boxes each input and tracker call and consumes output flags.

temporary_candidate_comparison.change: A fixed 32-point stack buffer cached pixel-scaled coordinates inside aperture().
temporary_candidate_comparison.status: reverted; not present in final source
temporary_candidate_comparison.method: Six baseline and six candidate binaries were run in alternating order with the same calibrated workload.
temporary_candidate_comparison.result: The candidate was slower in all six alternating pairs. Host load varied substantially, so no speedup claim is supported.

limitations: This measures Rust contour processing and tracker state only. It excludes camera capture, Vision, Swift scheduling, and display latency.
Input timestamps advance at 15 Hz, but the benchmark does not sleep between updates; elapsed time is CPU benchmark time, not a 15 fps end-to-end camera run.
Per-call samples include Instant timing overhead. The reported p95 is a sampled microbenchmark result, not a deadline guarantee under arbitrary load.
